success_patterns: Six of the eight answers were confirmed by passages that repeat the clue's own distinctive wording: a J!-Archive or flashcard line, a repeated quoted epithet, or a near-copy sentence. The agent copied the bare entity those passages tie to the clue (Joseph McCarthy, Punxsutawney Phil, Jamestown, Tennessee, Encyclopedia Brown).

A clue giving a quoted nickname or epithet ('America's Sherlock Holmes in Sneakers', 'Seer of Seers') was solved by finding the passages where that quoted phrase sits right beside a name. The agent then gave the name in the form those passages repeat, including the full form 'Punxsutawney Phil'.
A clue about a film 'series' with a named installment in the passages (Scream 3, Scream) was answered at the series level, 'Scream', not with the single film.

A clue giving a definition plus etymology ('Middle Dutch for little barrel... another way of saying yokel') was answered with the headword that the dictionary-style passages repeat in their entry titles ('Bumpkin').
Plain common-noun clues ('traditional color of London's double-decker buses') were answered with the bare noun ('red'), with no extra descriptor. This is already covered by the skill.

patch.reasoning: The verbatim-archive and bare-short-answer behaviours are already encoded and should not be touched. Three reusable reading strategies are not stated explicitly: (a) quoted epithet or nickname clues, where the repeated quote beside a name is the key; (b) series or franchise level, where the agent should not name a single installment; (c) definition-plus-etymology clues, where the answer is the dictionary headword in the entry titles. Each is a short, checkable instruction placed next to a related existing bullet, so net length grows very little.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - 'This film series / franchise / TV series / book series' asks for the SERIES name, not the single installment the passages happen to discuss. Drop sequel numerals and subtitles: passages about 'Scream 3' or 'Scream 2' -> 'Scream'. Choose the title that appears in every installment's name.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - QUOTED EPITHET / TITLE / NICKNAME in the clue ('America's Sherlock Holmes in Sneakers', '"Seer of Seers"'): search the passages for that same quoted phrase. The name written next to it, repeated across several passages, is the answer. Give it in the full form the passages repeat ('Punxsutawney Phil', 'Encyclopedia Brown'), without the epithet itself.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - DEFINITION + ETYMOLOGY clues ('From the Middle Dutch for "little barrel", it's another way of saying yokel'): the answer is the dictionary HEADWORD. Find the dictionary-style passages ('Define X', 'X - definition of X') whose entry text repeats the clue's etymology or synonyms, and answer with that headword in its basic form ('Bumpkin').
